Hi,

You can use sqlalchemy also without greenlet installed if you don't use the async parts.

Regarding how to fix this, I'm not sure if there is a better way of indicating where that dependency should be installed and where not. Already https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/6136 broke some external tools used as an alternative to pip (poetry) so it seems that all this stuff is really fragile.
We are open to suggestion regarding this!

After some more experimenting I found that I can get SQLAlchemy installed by using `pip install sqlalchemy --no-deps`, but that's not possible to do as part of a dependency (so I can't just do `pip install my-package-that-depends-on-sqlalchemy`), but it works as a work-around.

I guess the markers only support comparing with strings, and not a list of strings (which would solve the problem)?

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**replace "in" operator with "==" + "or" for greenlet platforms** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/3076

that above will work but it's awful.    @CaselIT note I am removing the "UPPERCASE" thing for platforms other than windows as im guessing that's just a windows thing.

reaching out to the pep-508 author: https://twitter.com/zzzeek/status/1437486584232910855
this should work for you in the next release

labels.name: setup
labels.description: issues related to installation and setup

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

This is a opposite issue of previous issue https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/7024

in short word, `platform_machine` is not a reliable env marker.

`platform_machine` is read from `platform.machine()`, and in windows, it may read from env variable which could be missing when installing, and it will return a empty string.

So greenlet will not be installed in some case

you can try the reproduction script in windows x64 or x86 (with .venv), and you will find `greenlet` is not installed


### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

_No response_

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

2.0.9

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

No

### Database Vendor and Major Version

No

### Python Version

3.11

### Operating system

Windows

### To Reproduce

```python
import os
import subprocess

print("python version:")
subprocess.run(
    ['python', '-V'],
    env={"PATH": os.environ.get("PATH")}
)

print("platform_version:")
subprocess.run(
    ['python', '-c', 'import platform;print(platform.machine())'],
    env={"PATH": os.environ.get("PATH")}
)

print("not install sqlalchemy:")
subprocess.run(
    ['./.venv/scripts/pip.exe', 'install', '-e', '.'],
    env={
            key: os.environ.get(key) for key in
            ['PATH', 'ALLUSERSPROFILE', 'VIRTUAL_ENV', 'WINDIR', 'TEMP', 'TMP',
             'APPDATA',
             'USERPROFILE', 'PROGRAMFILES', 'PROGRAMW6432']
        } | {name: value for name, value in os.environ.items() if value.startswith("C:")}
)

output = subprocess.getoutput(r'.\.venv\scripts\pip.exe freeze')

print("pip freeze:")
print(output.splitlines())

print("=====")
print("and you can't find greenlet")
```


### Error

No greenlet installed

### Additional context

_No response_
